Classroom Tech
BenQ Interactive Boards

Every classroom has a BenQ board. Here's everything you need to use it confidently.

⚡ Turning On & Off +

Press the power button on the lower-right of the board or use the remote. Always power down at the end of the day — hold the power button or use the remote's off button. The board will prompt you to confirm shut down.

🪪 Your BenQ Card +

Each teacher receives a personal BenQ NFC card. Tap it to the reader on the board to instantly load your saved profile, preferences, and apps. Keep this card with you — don't leave it in the room.

📡 Wireless Connection (ClickShare Dongle) +
  1. Plug the ClickShare dongle into a USB-A port on your laptop
  2. Launch the ClickShare app (or it may launch automatically)
  3. Click the button on the dongle — your screen mirrors instantly
  4. To stop sharing, click the dongle button again or unplug

If the dongle doesn't work, try the ClickShare desktop app from clickshare.barco.com

🔌 Wired Connection (HDMI) +

Find the HDMI cable at the board's connection panel (usually lower left side). Plug into your laptop — use a dongle adapter if your laptop has USB-C only. Switch the board's input to HDMI if it doesn't detect automatically.

✏️ Annotation & Touch +

The BenQ board supports multi-touch directly with your finger. Use the built-in stylus pen (stored in the board's pen tray) for finer annotation. The board's EZWrite app lets you write, draw, and annotate over any content. Annotations can be saved and shared with students.

☁️ Shared Spaces +

BenQ boards have a built-in Shared Space cloud feature. Students can contribute to the board from their devices in real time. Great for brainstorming, collaborative note-taking, and group work. Ask Jeremy Orr for a walkthrough of this feature.

📱 Apps on the Board +

BenQ boards run Android and have a curated set of educational apps pre-installed. You can also cast from your device using the ClickShare app. Contact Jeremy Orr to request additional apps for your board.

📞 Classroom Phones — Zoom Phone +

Every classroom is equipped with a Zoom Phone for internal and external calls. Your extension will be provided during orientation.

  • Log into the Zoom app on your computer or use the physical Zoom Phone device in your room
  • Dial internal extensions directly, or search the Zoom directory to find colleagues
  • For emergencies or admin needs, dial the main office extension
  • Voicemail transcripts are delivered automatically to your SRDS email

Contact Myron Toltsis at mtoltsis@saddleriverday.org for extension or setup issues.

💡 Pro tip: Arrive 10 minutes early before your first class to test your board connection. A little prep prevents a lot of scrambling.

MFPs & Printing

Multifunction printers across campus. Here's where to find them and how to use them.

Main Hall
2 MFPs
Upstairs faculty area & mail room
North Hall
2 MFPs
CIE (Center for Innovation & Entrepreneurship) and basement faculty lounge
Alford Hall
2 MFPs
Outside the Biology Lab
Walsh Hall
2 MFPs
Head of Upper School office and 2nd floor faculty lounge
🖨️ Standard Printing +
  1. Send your print job from your computer as usual
  2. Select the appropriate SRDS printer from your list
  3. Go to the MFP — your job will be in the queue
  4. Tap your name on the touchscreen to release and print

First time? Ask anyone on the tech team to install the correct print drivers on your laptop.

🔒 Secure Printing +

For sensitive documents, use the Secure Print feature. Your job is held in the queue until you physically authenticate at the printer — so no one else can pick up your documents. Select "Secure Print" in the print dialog and set a PIN.

📄 Scanning +
  1. Place your document on the glass or use the document feeder
  2. Tap Scan on the touchscreen
  3. Select Scan to Email — enter your SRDS email address
  4. Choose resolution and color settings
  5. Press Start — the scan arrives in your inbox within minutes
📎 SRDS has a thoughtful printing philosophy — we encourage digital-first wherever possible. Print mindfully!
LMS
Schoology

Your main hub for courses, assignments, gradebook, and student communication. Questions? Jeremy Orr runs training sessions — reach out to schedule one.

🚀 Getting Started +
  1. Go to app.schoology.com and sign in with your SRDS Google account
  2. Your courses should be pre-loaded — contact Jeremy Orr if anything is missing
  3. Set up a folder structure in each course before students arrive
  4. Customize your course profile and homepage
📝 Creating Assignments +
  1. Open your course → click Add Materials
  2. Choose Assignment, Page, Discussion, Quiz, or File/Link
  3. Set due date, points, and submission type
  4. Enable rubric or grading scale if needed
  5. Click Publish to make it visible to students immediately, or schedule it
📊 Gradebook +

The Schoology gradebook syncs with PowerSchool automatically. Enter grades directly in Schoology — they push to PowerSchool for report cards. Set your grading categories (classwork, homework, assessments, etc.) at the start of the year.

📣 Communication +

Use Announcements to push updates to all students in a course. Use Messages for direct communication with students and parents. Parents have real-time visibility into assignments and grades.

🧑‍💻 Questions about Schoology? Jeremy Orr is your go-to. Email jorr@saddleriverday.org to schedule a training session or walkthrough.
Student Info System
PowerSchool

Attendance, student records, and report card comments all live here.

✅ Taking Attendance +
  1. Log into PowerSchool Teacher portal (link in your email)
  2. Click on your class period
  3. Mark any absences or tardies at the start of class
  4. Submit — this is time-sensitive, do it within the first 10 minutes
  5. If you miss the window, contact the main office to correct the record
⚠️ Attendance must be taken at the start of every period. Late or missing attendance records require an admin correction.
📝 Report Card Comments +

Comments are entered in PowerSchool at the end of each marking period. The registrar sends reminders with the comment window open/close dates. Make sure your Schoology gradebook is current before the window opens so grades sync correctly.

👤 Student Records +

PowerSchool contains student contact info, schedule, emergency contacts, and historical records. Access this for legitimate educational purposes only, in accordance with FERPA guidelines.

Video Production
Rebel Vision Studio

A fully professional broadcast and film production suite. Whether you're producing a news segment, documentary, short film, or class project — the studio has everything you need.

📡 Broadcast & Studio +
  • TriCaster Switcher — professional live production switcher for multi-camera broadcasts, transitions, and overlays
  • Audio Board — full mixing console for live and recorded audio
  • Anchor Desk — broadcast-style news desk for on-camera presenting
  • Teleprompter — for polished, confident on-camera delivery
  • Green Screen — full chroma key backdrop for virtual backgrounds and compositing
🎥 Cameras & Capture +
  • Sony & Canon Cameras — professional cinema and DSLR cameras for studio and field shoots
  • GoPro Cameras — action and POV capture for dynamic, immersive footage
  • Drones — aerial photography and videography for outdoor projects
  • Wireless Microphones — lavalier and handheld for untethered audio capture
  • Phone Tripods — for mobile video capture and student-led projects
🎞️ Stabilization & Movement +
  • Tripods — standard and fluid-head for stable, locked-off shots
  • Steady Cams — body-mounted stabilization for smooth moving shots
  • Gimbals — electronic 3-axis stabilization for handheld and run-and-gun filming
🖥️ Post-Production +
  • Editing Workstations — Mac-based suites with full Adobe Creative Suite
  • Adobe Premiere Pro — professional video editing
  • Adobe After Effects — motion graphics and visual effects
  • Adobe Audition — audio mixing and cleanup
  • Lighting Kits — studio and portable lighting for any environment
📅 Booking & Equipment Loans +

To schedule studio time or borrow equipment for a classroom project, contact Laura Hollis at lhollis@saddleriverday.org. Equipment loans require a return agreement and must be checked out through the tech department.

📎 View the Rebel Vision Resource Guide →

🎬 Not sure how to incorporate video production into your subject? Documentary projects, news-style reports, and student-produced content work across every discipline. Laura Hollis is happy to co-plan.
IDEAS Lab
Making & Fabrication

The IDEAS Lab is a full makerspace with professional fabrication tools. You don't need to be a tech teacher to bring these into your curriculum — Jeremy Orr can help you design the right project.

🖨️ Bambu Lab H2D — 3D Printing (×3) +

Three Bambu Lab H2D printers — fast, high-quality, multi-material capable. Great for rapid prototyping and detailed student projects.

  1. Design: Use TinkerCAD (browser-based) or Gravity Sketch (VR)
  2. Export: Save as .STL or .3MF file
  3. Slice: Open Bambu Studio on the lab computer and send to printer
  4. Print: Choose filament color — multiple options available
  5. Collect: 30 min to several hours depending on complexity
⚡ Glowforge — Laser Cutter & Engraver +

Precisely cuts and engraves wood, acrylic, leather, cardboard, fabric, and more. ⚠️ Requires faculty supervision at all times — get certified with Jeremy Orr before your first use.

  • Cut: Wood, acrylic, leather, cardboard, fabric
  • Engrave: Wood, acrylic, glass, anodized metal, stone
  • Great for: Custom awards, architectural models, signage, science specimens, portfolio pieces
✂️ Cricut — Cutting & Crafting +

Precisely cuts vinyl, paper, cardstock, iron-on, sticker paper, and more. Design in Cricut Design Space (browser-based, free account required).

  • Vinyl & iron-on — labels, posters, custom apparel
  • Paper & cardstock — cards, covers, dioramas, pop-ups
  • Sticker paper — student-designed stickers and branding
🎓 Cross-Curricular Ideas +
  • Science: 3D molecular models, laser-engraved specimens, topographic maps
  • Math: Geometric solids, custom manipulatives, laser-cut puzzles
  • History: Architectural models, artifacts, map terrain
  • Art: Sculptures, jewelry, laser-engraved prints, vinyl installations
  • ELA: Story props, character models, custom book covers
  • Engineering: Full prototype-test-iterate design challenges
📅 Booking the IDEAS Lab +

Contact Jeremy Orr to schedule class time. He can run an orientation for you and your students — highly recommended before your first session with any machine.

Policies
SRDS AI Policy

You set the tone for AI use in your classroom. Here's what our policy says — and what it means in practice.

Ethics & Accountability
No hate, no plagiarism
Students must not use AI to promote violence, hate, or discrimination. Using AI to plagiarize — including rephrasing others' work — carries the same consequences as academic dishonesty.
Privacy & Security
No personal data in AI
Students must never enter personal, identifying, or sensitive information into AI tools. Most platforms retain user data. Treat AI prompts as semi-public.
Appropriate Use
Teacher decides
AI may only be used when you explicitly permit it — in your syllabus or assignment description. You retain full authority over AI use in your classroom.
Verify & Disclose
Always fact-check. Always disclose.
AI-generated content must be verified with reliable sources. Students must clearly disclose AI use in their work. Failure to disclose = failing grade on that assignment.
"Teaching students how to think, not what to think."
SRDS Motto — the foundation of our approach to AI
🤝 Want to thoughtfully incorporate AI into your teaching? Connect with Jeremy Orr or Laura Hollis — we love talking about this and can help you design assignments that work with or around AI.
